QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_25

question.text: 'Marine Category II AIF' and its affiliate PMS house share the same office premises. To avoid information leakage and conflicts between fund management and advisory verticals, the manager should establish:

answer.text: Common trading terminals shared by all employees
'Chinese walls' — information barriers segregating teams handling potentially conflicting assignments
An annual picnic for the combined team

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chinese walls are formal information barriers separating teams to protect confidentiality and prevent insider information flow between AIF-manager, PMS, proprietary-trading, and other affiliated entities. The PDF lists Chinese walls under 'Role of Human Capital in avoiding conflicts'. **The Trap:** Open-plan and common terminals INCREASE conflict risk. Picnic is distractor humor. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XXI-B (Portfolio Manager), X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser), XV (Research Analyst), III-A/C (Compliance) all test Chinese walls. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Chinese walls are audited during CTR — document: (i) physical access logs, (ii) system-level data segregation, (iii) pre-clearance for cross-wall communications, (iv) annual declarations from staff.
